title: NEXA — Real-time Video Analytics Platform
oneLiner: Production platform that turns live CCTV into real-time AI alerts — I built its camera-processing core and GPU model-serving layer.
objective: NEXA turns live CCTV into real-time alerts: camera feeds pass through AI models on GPU servers, and a rule engine raises alerts with video evidence and a live view. It runs for UK clients, including a 200+ camera Premier League stadium, across Google Cloud and on-site UK servers, built by a team of 10+ engineers.
achievements: Designed and built the camera-processing service: one process per camera that reads the stream, picks frames, runs its AI pipelines, tracks people and raises alerts. Its plug-in framework hosts 20+ detection pipelines built by me and 6 other engineers.
Built the shared GPU model-serving layer: up to 16 stateless model workers behind one request/response format, so one loaded model serves many cameras.
Built the alerting path — one alert per incident, per-person deduplication, a clip from before each incident, back-pressure — and moved it from Kafka to Redis Streams with no lost alerts.
On a lab server, raised cameras per server 4× (~4 → 16) by moving 12 models to NVIDIA Triton + TensorRT and decoding video on the GPU. Production rollout planned.
Sized edge and cloud hardware by load-testing to failure: 8 cameras per Jetson Orin Nano (bound by its hardware video decoder, not compute) and 10 per cloud T4 server.
Made small weapons detectable at CCTV distance with person-focused tiled detection that zooms in only around people.
Found and fixed a 31-hour silent outage where camera processes leaked network connections until AI results stopped while every dashboard stayed green.
Built an MLflow model registry with promotion, rollback and checksum-verified model delivery to every server.
